summary: The bill expands the SBA Office of Advocacy's statutory functions to include the international economy and adds a new duty to represent small businesses' interests before foreign governments and international entities on regulatory and trade matters.

scores.thoughts: The bill clarifies and slightly expands the duties of an existing SBA office focused on small business advocacy. No appropriations, funding changes, or spending directives are included, so it has no bearing on government spending levels.
The legislation addresses only the functions of the Office of Advocacy and makes no changes to tax law, rates, or policy.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, regulation, or markets.
The bill contains nothing concerning firearms, regulations, or rights.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not address reproductive health, abortion access, or related regulations.
No military, defense, or national security spending or policy changes are present.
The legislation makes no reference to environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy standards.
Nothing in the bill affects welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
The text does not engage with schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
The bill contains no criminal justice, sentencing, or policing reforms.

The bill adds a duty for the Office of Advocacy to represent small businesses before foreign governments and international entities on regulatory and trade initiatives. While this touches trade, it is purely procedural advocacy without directing any substantive policy shift toward free trade or protectionism.
No deficit, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy provisions are included.
The legislation does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No foreign assistance or aid programs are mentioned.
The bill has no connection to voting rights, election procedures, or voter ID.
Nothing in the text concerns technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill does not alter labor law, union rights, or employer obligations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, anti-discrimination rules, or related civil rights balances.
